chronology: Recap: Aghnar destroyed Jejoh and the elder witches, losing an arm; Oda left spiritually devastated after their shared mental battle; six Cetacyborgs still guard the asteroid.

Tonto recounts aftermath: Oda's soul had already departed, making conventional brain surgery unnecessary; Klawoutai bids farewell to his messiah (the little white ape) on a mushroom-covered ice asteroid.
A biomechanical entity threatens two incapacitated humans with the end of the Metabarons clan.
A space battle against tentacled biomechanical entities; an unidentified rescuer intervenes, destroys several enemies, calls Aghnar by name, and urges psychic union.
Aghnar's ship drawn in by tractor beam into a mechanical chamber; a cloaked woman orders robots withdrawn before he will approach; he tends to his injured beloved.
The cloaked woman reveals herself as Honorata using scent and the memory of Okkhar's carnivorous flowers; Aghnar insists he witnessed her death in a Shabda-Oud bombing.

Tonto explains Honorata's survival: she pushed her psychic shabda-ud power to its limit, opened a time fissure at the Maxiprotonic Tower at age 30, spent 20 subjective years inside, emerged at age 50 with a new beating heart, then reached the fortress tower in 16.09 seconds.
At Chrono-G (the punctual Pradex point), inside a temporal fissure, Honorata and her assistants spend years studying how to safely remove a heart-bomb; the patient enters psycho-cellular catalepsy.

Honorata Lao undergoes high-risk heart transplant; replacement heart from an Arcturian Katria agent begins beating; a vessel is built over five years for revenge against Shabda-Oud; two children vow to avenge their mother.

Honorata confronts Aghnar aboard her ship, explaining she hid her survival to protect them from enemies capable of detecting emotion; she claims she deliberately preserved his grief and hatred to drive him toward destroying the Shabda-Oud.
Aghnar presents Oda as a living cadaver, blaming the Marges; Honorata offers her knowledge of Shabda-Oud psycho-surgical science and requests Tonto as assistant; she vows Oda will live.

Honorata prepares a dangerous deep mental probe; forces Aghnar to choose between her and Oda; Aghnar chooses Oda and rejects the Metabaron warrior identity, declaring the Castakas will continue differently.
Aghnar receives a protonic prosthetic arm; Oda is revived from her catatonic state; Aghnar and Oda recognize each other, able only to speak each other's names.
Steelhead is conceived during Aghnar and Oda's reunion; identified by the narrator as grandfather of the present Metabaron.
Aghnar recovers his intellect; Honorata sequesters herself in the south gallery with only Tonto; Aghnar and Oda spend nine months in near-happiness, divided over whether to raise a warrior heir.
Oda gives birth to a bio-male son; Aghnar announces the birth to Honorata, who appears nightly for only thirty seconds before retreating.
A small robot inadvertently exposes Honorata's deception: she had been moving a corpse to make Aghnar believe his mother was appearing alive; Aghnar forces his way toward Honorata's chamber.
Aghnar accuses the woman holding his infant of being Honorata in Oda's body; declares Oda dead, her cells overwritten by a Lota-linked virus; condemns the infant as incestuous and demands the child.
A long-haired figure unleashes a devastating energy beam that tears through the mechanical interior.
The infant is caught in an energy exchange against a cybernetic attacker and is decapitated; an augmented figure protests the killing and argues the child should have been grafted to a machine.

A panicked mother carries the surviving infant to Tonto; the infant is grafted onto Tonto's back and sustained by his internal circuits; a steel head will be grafted when the child reaches adult size, giving rise to Steelhead; Aghnar departs vowing to become the most merciless Metabaron and return to duel the grown child.
locations: Witches' asteroid: site of prior battle against Jejoh and elder witches, recap setting
Ice asteroid with mushroom-filled city: Klawoutai's home, ape-populated, spores from female apes' goitres grow giant mushrooms
Outer space battle zone: Aghnar fights tentacled biomechanical entities and is rescued by an unknown figure
Honorata's mechanical chamber: pipe-filled interior with robot attendants, reached via tractor beam
Maxiprotonic Tower: where Honorata opened the time fissure enabling her survival
Chrono-G / Pradex punctual point: temporal fissure laboratory used for the heart-bomb surgery
Metabunker: mobile base from which Aghnar's family departed; Tonto operates here
South gallery: Honorata's sequestration quarters during her long post-procedure recovery
Surgical and medical chambers: multiple high-tech rooms used for heart transplant, mental probe, arm grafting, and infant grafting
Hangar or launch bay: departure point after the infant is grafted onto Tonto
lore_laws: The Shabda-Oud are associated with breeding programs, psycho-surgical science, and heart-bombs that explode if removed incorrectly.
A practitioner of psychic shabda-ud power at its extreme can open a time fissure; Chrono-G, the punctual Pradex point, is the designated location for this.
Inside a time fissure a subject's personal time accelerates dramatically relative to outside observers; extended exposure produces psycho-cellular catalepsy.
A living body can be kept alive by physically grafting it onto another body, sustained by the host's internal circuits.
Tonto is a machine whose internal circuits can serve as life support for an attached organic body.
Seven C-T cyborgs can only be defeated if their weak spot is known; without that knowledge they are considered unbeatable.
Female apes carry spores in their goitres that generate giant mushrooms when released on an ice asteroid surface.
Honorata possessed psychic sonar capable of detecting emotional states and foreseeing deaths; hostile entities can also detect strong emotions to locate targets.
The Metabaron clan tradition requires a ritual duel between the reigning Metabaron and the next-generation heir.
Grafting a steel head onto an heir is a named rite tied to the identity Steelhead.
Magon apes can be deployed as a swarm force from a Cetacyborg under mental command.
major_events: Honorata revealed alive to Aghnar after years believed dead, having survived through a time fissure at the Maxiprotonic Tower and a subsequent heart transplant.
Honorata performs psycho-surgery on Oda using Shabda-Oud techniques with Tonto as assistant, successfully reviving Oda from a catatonic state.
Aghnar forced to choose between Honorata and Oda; chooses Oda and formally rejects the Metabaron warrior identity, declaring the Castakas will continue on different terms.
Aghnar and Oda conceive Steelhead, who is identified as grandfather of the present Metabaron.
A robot exposes Honorata's long-running deception: she had been animating a corpse to appear alive to Aghnar.
Aghnar declares Oda dead and accuses Honorata of occupying Oda's body after cloning herself within her using a Lota-linked virus.
The infant son is near-fatally injured in a violent confrontation involving energy blasts and a cybernetic attacker.
The infant is grafted onto Tonto's back to survive; destined to be called Steelhead once a steel head is grafted at adulthood; Aghnar departs promising a future duel with the grown child.
open_uncertainties: Whether the woman Aghnar confronts holding the infant is truly Honorata inhabiting Oda's body or still Oda; the accusation is Aghnar's and is not independently verified by the pages.
The exact mechanism by which the Lota-linked virus allegedly overwrote every cell of Oda's body is not explained.
The identity of the mysterious rescuer who saves Aghnar in the space battle and calls for psychic union is never explicitly named on these pages.
The identity and nature of the hostile biomechanical entity that declares the end of the Metabarons clan is not confirmed.
The true nature of the little white ape and the prophecy of a journey from a fog world to a diamond planet are introduced but not resolved within this volume.
The exact spelling of the Arcturian Katria agent whose heart was transplanted into Honorata Lao is uncertain due to small text resolution.
Printed page numbers visible in the scanned images do not consistently match the supplied page labels, suggesting possible pagination discrepancies in this edition.
recurring_motifs: Sacrifice for clan survival: characters mutilate, isolate, or endanger themselves repeatedly to preserve the Metabaron lineage.
Deception within the family: Honorata hides her survival, manipulates Aghnar's grief, and is accused of occupying Oda's body.
Psychic and mental combat: inner battles, mental probes, and psychic powers drive key turning points.
Biomechanical transformation as destiny: prosthetics, heart transplants, body grafting, and the steel-head rite mark each generation.
Revenge against the Shabda-Oud as a multigenerational engine motivating sacrifice and strategy.
Tonto as machine narrator and witness who holds memory and ultimately becomes a living incubator for Steelhead.
The Metabunker as mobile home base and symbol of dynastic continuity.
title: The Possession of Oda
